items.title: Heat killed ‘staggering’ 50,000 people in Europe’s cities this summer, scientists warn
items.author: Ajit Niranjan
items.summary: New research indicates that record-breaking summer heat in European cities resulted in 50,000 deaths, with scientists attributing 65% of these fatalities to anthropogenic climate change.

brief.what: A study modeling heat-related mortality across 854 European cities found that 50,000 people died this summer due to extreme temperatures. brief.who: The study was conducted by climate and health scientists, including Malcolm Mistry, with observations provided by emergency medical professionals like Mario Guarino.
brief.context: The research utilized historical relationships between heat and health to model mortality across urban areas, which house approximately 40% of the European population. brief.why: Scientists attribute the rising death toll to climate breakdown caused by greenhouse gas emissions, which have warmed Europe twice as fast as the global average. Factors such as poverty, loneliness, and lack of access to air conditioning were cited as exacerbating the health risks for vulnerable populations.
brief.next: Doctors are urging governments to reduce fossil fuel consumption, improve health systems, and implement urban cooling strategies to mitigate future heat-related tragedies.
